requirement:
Model tool descriptions SHOULD NOT explain cases the model meets only
occasionally, such as access policy, excluded or build-output paths, redaction,
paging, and failures, and the harness SHOULD explain each of these where it
occurs: in the tool error, or in a note in the result it affects. The model reads
every description on every assessment, so explaining rare cases there costs
attention on every review for a case most never meet, and access-policy wording
in particular can steer its reasoning away from the review. A tool whose purpose
is one of these cases, such as `next_page`, explains it in its description.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover both halves of `requirements.authoring.tool_descriptions.special_cases`, and I found no gap.

**Descriptions must not explain rare cases (SHOULD NOT).**
- `tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[descriptions_leave_paging_policy_redaction_and_failures_to_results]` scans every tool description, case-insensitively, for a list of rare-case phrases. The list covers paging ("kib", "returned in pages"), redaction ("redact", "credential"), access policy ("denied", "disallow", "habeas.toml", "aborts", "untracked", "policy", "permitted"), build output and excluded paths ("build output", "ignore rules", "exclusion"), outside-project paths ("outside the project") and failures ("tool error"). The test fails if any description contains one.
- `tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[descriptions_give_each_argument_and_the_result_form]` also checks the descriptions. It requires the common-case content, so the descriptions stay useful without the special cases.
- This is a phrase-based check, so a description could still explain a rare case in wording the list doesn't contain, such as "paged" instead of "returned in pages". I treat that as acceptable for a SHOULD NOT that has no precise boundary.

**The `next_page` exception.**
- The same test asserts the exact `next_page` parameter schema.
- `descriptions_give_each_argument_and_the_result_form` requires the `next_page` description to contain "following page", "same shape", the token wording and an opaque-token note. That is, the tool whose purpose is paging explains paging itself.

**The harness explains each case where it occurs.**
- **Access policy:**
  - `tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[untracked_diagnostics_name_git_add_and_an_allow_rule]` checks that denial errors for habeas and list_files name the path, `git add` and the `habeas.toml allow rule`. It also checks that the harness changes nothing.
  - `tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors]` checks the "outside the project" error across the tools. It also checks that a matching disallow still aborts.
  - `access.rs#mod[tests]/fn[evidence_rules_are_literal_paths_not_globs]` checks that a disallow rule produces a "disallowed by habeas.toml rule" error.
  - `mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_read_through_a_symlink_leaving_the_project_returns_an_error_to_the_model]` checks that the denial reaches the model, naming the path and reason.
- **Excluded and build-output paths:**
  - `tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]` checks the "generated evidence" error across all five tools, including through symlinks.
  - `tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requests_for_book_or_target_output_are_ordinary_read_failures]` checks that `book`, the build-dir and `target` return an error containing "holds build output" and "the sources it is built from are elsewhere in the project". It also checks that `book` stays readable when a build-dir is set.
- **Redaction:** `tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[only_results_with_redacted_text_carry_the_redaction_note]` checks that `REDACTION_NOTE` appears on redacted habeas and ripgrep results. It checks the note is absent when nothing was redacted, including when the source contains literal marker text.
- **Paging:** `pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[large_listings_and_outlines_page_whole_entries_in_order]` uses the helper `all_pages`. The helper asserts that every page with a successor carries `PAGE_NOTE` ("call next_page with this page's next token") and that the last page has no `next`.
- **Failures:** `mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[malformed_and_failed_reads_return_to_the_model_and_the_assessment_continues]` covers malformed arguments, a missing file, an absent item and an out-of-range line. In each case the error text is absent from the first request and present in the second, and the assessment continues. It also asserts the failure is not a PermissionDenied abort.

**Conclusion.** Every clause has a test that exercises the behavior and asserts the outcome. All the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.
